- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast rise to 5–7% above prior peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 85–90), model overestimates future highs; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% per day.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00) and price history shows volatility, model tends to smooth too much; allow 1–3% noise in forecast to capture short-term swings.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 1–2% upward adjustment if last 3–5 days show rising volatility or sentiment shift.
- If sentiment history shows increasing positive sentiment (e.g., 0.2 → 0.4 → 0.6), model may overreact; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.
